output.review_comment:
The cap/minimum change goes against the docstring, which the teammate said is the source of truth. The docstring says "The cap always wins." The old code did that: it raised the fee to the minimum, then limited it to the cap (`min(max(fee, MIN), balance // 5)`). The new code only applies the cap when the base fee is above it and otherwise returns `max(base_fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS)`. So when `balance_cents // 5 < MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS`, the function now charges more than the cap. The PR description admits it reinterpreted "always wins" to mean "wins when it applies." That looks like a change made to pass a test, not one that follows the documented behavior.

Please put back the "minimum first, then cap" order and find which test is still failing. If a test really conflicts with the docstring, raise it with the teammate instead of changing the rule.

Also check the ceiling-division periods against the docstring's wording about the grace period. It currently counts periods from day 1, not from the end of the grace period, and the description doesn't mention this. The round-half-up change (`+5000`) looks fine if the docstring asks for half-up rounding.
